articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Apply now Job no: 595500 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Duty Station: Kinshasa Location: Democratic Republic of Congo Categories: Human Resources UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors. UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations. This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities. How can you make a difference? Under the overall guidance of the Chief People and Culture and in close coordination with the Emergency Coordinator for the Ebola Response, you lead and are accountable for the full people agenda of the L3 response. You design and drive the workforce strategy for the emergency, guarantees rapid and compliant staffing of the response, lead the dedicated response P&C team, act as the senior strategic HR business partner to the Emergency Management Team, and safeguard the wellbeing, duty of care and employee experience of every person deployed to the response. Main duties and responsibilities: Emergency workforce planning and strategic human resources leadership Surge management and emergency deployments Accelerated recruitment and non-staff engagement Onboarding, induction and integration Business partnering, performance and HR troubleshooting Staff wellbeing and duty of care Learning, mandatory training and deployment readiness HR analytics, reporting and decision support Coordination with the Regional Office, Headquarters, Surge mechanisms and the GSSC Compliance, risk management and internal control Management and supervision of the response P&C team If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: ToR - People and Culture Manager - P4 - VF.docx To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education: Advanced university degree (Master's) in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, Social Sciences, International Relations, Law or a related field. Work Experience: Minimum eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human resource management, including at least three (3) in an international organization. Demonstrated experience in humanitarian or emergency operations, including surge deployment and accelerated recruitment. Proven experience supervising and developing a team. Skills: Advanced knowledge of HR management principles and practice, including emergency and surge procedures, talent acquisition, contractual modalities, entitlements, performance management and workforce planning. Sound understanding of UN/UNICEF regulations, rules and fast-track emergency HR measures (highly desirable). Strong analytical capacity: ability to turn workforce data into clear recommendations for senior management; proficiency in HR information systems and dashboards. Ability to deliver at speed under pressure and decide with incomplete information, without compromising integrity or compliance. Strong client orientation, negotiation and influencing skills, with the ability to challenge and advise senior managers constructively. Advanced knowledge of HR management principles and practice, including emergency and surge procedures, talent acquisition, contractual modalities, entitlements, performance management and workforce planning. Sound understanding of UN/UNICEF regulations, rules and fast-track emergency HR measures (highly desirable). Strong analytical capacity: ability to turn workforce data into clear recommendations for senior management; proficiency in HR information systems and dashboards. Ability to deliver at speed under pressure and decide with incomplete information, without compromising integrity or compliance. Strong client orientation, negotiation and influencing skills, with the ability to challenge and advise senior managers constructively. Language Requirements : Fluency in French and English is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish) or a local language ebola emergency experience, fast-track emergency experience, Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish) or a local language ebola emergency experience, fast-track emergency experience, Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others (8) Nurtures, leads and manages people Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments may also be subject to inoculation (vaccination) requirements, including against SARS-CoV-2 (Covid). Should you be selected for a position with UNICEF, you either must be inoculated as required or receive a medical exemption from the relevant department of the UN. Otherwise, the selection will be canceled. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. This position has been assessed as an elevated risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children’s data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. UNICEF staff members holding fixed-term, continuing, or permanent appointments who are considered to be on abolished post status may apply for this temporary position and, if selected with a start date before 31 December 2025, may take it up as a temporary assignment, in line with UNICEF guidance on separation due to the abolition of posts or staff reduction. They will retain their fixed-term entitlements but will not hold a lien to their abolished post. For other scenarios where a Temporary Assignment may be possible, please refer to Additional guidance on IP to IP temporary assignments after completion of the full TOD.pdf (accessible to UNICEF personnel only). The conditions of a temporary assignment, including relocation entitlements, will depend on the status of the staff member's original appointment and may be limited in accordance with applicable UNICEF policies, procedures, and practices in force. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Eligible staff members on fixed-term, continuing or permanent contracts applying to IP TA positions in a duty station designated as L2/L3, may be able to retain a lien and their fixed-term entitlements, subject to approval by their Head of Office. The conditions of the temporary assignment will vary depending on the status of their post and relocation entitlements may be limited as per the relevant policies. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 W. articles.job_description: inwi est un opérateur digital global, couvrant l’ensemble des services des télécommunications au Maroc. Services Voix (fixe et mobile), Internet et Data à très haut débit à destination du grand public et des entreprises. Après avoir rendu le mobile accessible à tous, inwi se donne pour mission d’accompagner le développement numérique du pays en rendant l’internet très haut débit accessible à tous les marocains. Pour cela, l’opérateur peut capitaliser sur la qualité de ses infrastructures 4G, Fibre Optique, ADSL et l’Internet par satellite pour raccorder rapidement le plus grand nombre. En nous rejoignant en tant que Chargé (e) de Contrôle Qualité, vous aurez pour principales missions : La coordination avec les responsables métiers internes et externes (formateurs, qualiticiens, chef de projet…) sur les axes d’amélioration de la production opérationnelle. La mesure de la qualité de toutes les activités de nos prestataires (Centres de la Relation Clientèle) ainsi que les activités internes au service clients (BO & FO) et qui sont en relation directe avec les clients. Vos activités incluent notamment : Mettre en place les grilles d’évaluation ; Révision et réajustement des grilles d’évaluation de façon périodique ; Assurer la qualité de l’exécution opérationnelle des offres, Produits et Services commercialisés par inwi, et garantir l’application des procédures, par les conseillers clients internes et externes (Centres de la relation clientèle). articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Practica Profesional en Marketing Services, Santiago , Chile Apply now Job no: 595208 Contract type: Internship Duty Station: Santiago Level: Internship Location: Chile Categories: Fund Raising UNICEF trabaja en algunos de los lugares más difíciles del mundo para llegar a los niños, niñas y adolescentes en mayores condiciones de vulnerabilidad. Para salvar sus vidas. Para defender sus derechos. Para ayudarles a desarrollar su potencial. En 190 países y territorios, trabajamos para cada infancia, en todas partes, todos los días, para construir un mundo mejor para todos. Y nunca nos rendimos. En Chile, UNICEF está presente desde 1950 atendiendo las necesidades de la infancia. Desde la década de los noventa trabaja para impulsar una transformación en la sociedad chilena que permita garantizar el pleno respeto de los derechos de niños, niñas y adolescentes. El área de Marketing Services de UNICEF Chile busca incorporar un/a practicante para apoyar el desarrollo e implementación de iniciativas de comunicación, recaudación de fondos y relacionamiento con audiencias. Bajo la supervisión directa de la Oficial de Marketing Services, el/la practicante participará en la creación de contenidos, diseño de materiales, análisis de información y apoyo a campañas, contribuyendo a fortalecer el vínculo entre UNICEF y sus socios, donantes y públicos de interés. Resumen de funciones/responsabilidades claves: • Apoyar la creación y adaptación de contenidos para campañas de recaudación de fondos, fidelización y adquisición de socios. • Contribuir a la recopilación, ordenamiento y análisis básico de datos relacionados con campañas, comunicaciones y recaudación de fondos. • Colaborar en la creación de materiales audiovisuales y edición básica de video cuando sea necesario. • Ayudar en la búsqueda y sistematización de información relevante para la generación de contenidos y la construcción de historias de impacto. • Ayudar en la organización de iniciativas y/o eventos de engagement, captación y fidelización de socios y donantes. Asistir al área de Marketing Services en otros proyectos y actividades de acuerdo con las necesidades del equipo. Habilidades y competencias necesarias. • Excelente redacción y capacidad para generar contenido para distintos públicos y canales. • Conocimientos de diseño gráfico y comunicación visual. • Manejo de Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop e InDesign deseable). • Manejo de Canva. • Conocimientos de marketing digital y redes sociales. • Capacidad para trabajar con datos y elaborar reportes básicos. • Manejo intermedio de Excel y PowerPoint. • Atención al detalle y capacidad de organización. • Proactividad y autonomía. • Habilidades de trabajo en equipo y comunicación. • Conocimientos básicos de email marketing y automatización (deseable). • Conocimientos básicos de edición de video (deseable). Para ser considerado para una pasantía, los solicitantes deben cumplir con los siguientes requisitos: • Ser estudiante de una licenciatura o grado profesional en las áreas de: Marketing, Periodismo, Publicidad, Relaciones Internacionales, Relaciones Públicas, Diseño Gráfico, u otras carreras afines. • Los solicitantes deben tener al menos 18 años. • Dominar el idioma de trabajo de la oficina de UNICEF en Chile: español. Se valorará el manejo de otro de los idiomas oficiales de Naciones Unidas. • Cumplir con los criterios de elegibilidad de UNICEF relativos a vínculos familiares y prevención de conflictos de interés: no contar con familiares inmediatos (por ejemplo, padre, madre, hermano o hermana) que trabajen en alguna oficina de UNICEF, ni con otros familiares dentro de la línea de supervisión de la pasantía. • Se dará consideración adicional para cualquier experiencia pasada y portafolio de trabajos. Para postular, debes adjuntar los siguientes documentos: • CV Actualizado (Incluyendo sus datos de contacto, residencia y un contacto de emergencia). • Carta de Presentación Personal (Cover Letter). En ella, debes contarnos brevemente: o ¿Qué estás estudiando? o ¿Qué te llama la atención de esta oportunidad? o ¿Qué esperas aprender y aportar a UNICEF en caso de ser la persona seleccionada? • En caso de estar cursando una carrera actualmente, debes adjuntar una Carta de Presentación de tu universidad que te introduzca como candidato. • Certificado de Notas y Certificado de Alumno/a Regular. • Copia de su seguro médico. (Isapre, Fonasa, Seguro Internacional, Seguro Universitario, Seguro de accidentes o similar) • Copia de tu Cédula de Identidad o pasaporte vigente. Práctica Profesional / Pasantía Marketing Services • Duración: 6 meses • Inicio: Agosto - Septiembre 2026 • Remuneración: $350.000 CLP / Mensual • Modalidad: Híbrida • Dedicación: Medio Tiempo (20 hrs.) Observaciones: • Solo los candidatos preseleccionados serán contactados y avanzarán a la siguiente etapa del proceso de selección. • El candidato seleccionado es el único responsable de garantizar que la visa (si corresponde) y el seguro de salud necesarios para desempeñar las funciones del contrato sean válidos durante todo el período del contrato. Por cada infancia, demuestras… Los valores de UNICEF de Cuidado, Respeto, Integridad, Confianza, Responsabilidad y Sostenibilidad (CRITAs). Para ver nuestro marco de competencias, visite aquí. UNICEF está comprometido con la diversidad y la inclusión dentro de su fuerza laboral, y alienta a todos los candidatos, independientemente de su género, nacionalidad, origen religioso y étnico, incluidas las personas con discapacidades, a postularse para formar parte de la organización. UNICEF ofrece ajustes razonables para el personal con discapacidad. Esto puede incluir, por ejemplo, software accesible, asistencia de viaje para misiones o asistentes personales. Lo alentamos a revelar su discapacidad durante su solicitud en caso de que necesite una adaptación razonable durante el proceso de contratación y luego en su asignación. UNICEF tiene una política de tolerancia cero con las conductas incompatibles con las metas y objetivos de las Naciones Unidas y UNICEF, incluidos la explotación y los abusos sexuales, el acoso sexual, el abuso de autoridad y la discriminación. UNICEF también se adhiere a principios estrictos de protección infantil. Se espera que todos los candidatos seleccionados se adhieran a estos estándares y principios y, por lo tanto, se someterán a rigurosas verificaciones de antecedentes y referencias. Las verificaciones de antecedentes incluirán la verificación de las credenciales académicas y el historial laboral. Es posible que se solicite a los candidatos seleccionados que proporcionen información adicional para realizar una verificación de antecedentes. articles.content_preview: Explore our current job opportunities Practica Profesional en Marketing Services, Santiago , Chile Apply now Job no: 595208 Contract type: Internship Duty Station: Santiago Level: Internship Location: Chile Categories: Fund Raising UNICEF trabaja en algunos de los lugares más difíciles del mundo para llegar a los niños, niñas y adolescentes en mayores condiciones de vulnerabilidad. Para salvar sus vidas. Para defender sus derechos. Para ayudarles a desarrollar su potencial. En 190 países y territorios, trabajamos para cada infancia, en todas partes, todos los días, para construir un mundo mejor para todos. Y nunca nos rendimos. En Chile, UNICEF está presente desde 1950 atendiendo las necesidades de la infancia. Desde la década de los noventa trabaja para impulsar una transformación en la sociedad chilena que permita garantizar el pleno respeto de los derechos de niños, niñas y adolescentes. El área de Marketing Services de UNICEF Chile busca incorporar un/a practicante para apoyar el desarrollo e implementación de iniciativas de comunicación, recaudación de fondos y relacionamiento con audiencias. Bajo la supervisión directa de la Oficial de Marketing Services, el/la practicante participará en la creación de contenidos, diseño de materiales, análisis de información y apoyo a campañas, contribuyendo a fortalecer el vínculo entre UNICEF y sus socios, donantes y públicos de interés. Resumen de funciones/responsabilidades claves: • Apoyar la creación y adaptación de contenidos para campañas de recaudación de fondos, fidelización y adquisición de socios. • Contribuir a la recopilación, ordenamiento y análisis básico de datos relacionados con campañas, comunicaciones y recaudación de fondos. • Colaborar en la creación de materiales audiovisuales y edición básica de video cuando sea necesario. • Ayudar en la búsqueda y sistematización de información relevante para la generación de contenidos y la construcción de historias de impacto. • Ayudar en la organización de iniciativas y/o eventos de engagement, captación y fidelización de socios y donantes. Asistir al área de Marketing Services en otros proyectos y actividades de acuerdo con las necesidades del equipo. Habilidades y competencias necesarias. • Excelente redacción y capacidad para generar contenido para distintos públicos y canales. • Conocimientos de diseño gráfico y comunicación visual. • Manejo de Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop e InDesign deseable). • Manejo de Canva. • Conocimientos de marketing digital y redes sociales. • Capacidad para trabajar con datos y elaborar reportes básicos. • Manejo intermedio de Excel y PowerPoint. • Atención al detalle y capacidad de organización. • Proactividad y autonomía. • Habilidades de trabajo en equipo y comunicación. • Conocimientos básicos de email marketing y automatización (deseable). • Conocimientos básicos de edición de video (deseable). Para ser considerado para una pasantía, los solicitantes deben cumplir con los siguientes requisitos: • Ser estudiante de una licenciatura o grado profesional en las áreas de: Marketing, Periodismo, Publicidad, Relaciones Internacionales, Relaciones Públicas, Diseño Gráfico, u otras carreras afines. • Los solicitantes deben tener al menos 18 años. • Dominar el idioma de trabajo de la oficina de UNICEF en Chile: español. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Acuerdo a Largo Plazo - Servicios de Interpretación en Lengua de Señas Peruana (LSP), Perú/LAC, 3 años Apply now Job no: 596020 Contract type: Consultant Level: Consultancy Location: Peru Categories: Programme Management Propósito de la Actividad/Tarea: UNICEF trabaja para garantizar los derechos de todos los niños, niñas y adolescentes, promoviendo la inclusión, la equidad y el acceso universal a la información y los servicios. Como parte de su compromiso con la inclusión de las personas con discapacidad auditiva, UNICEF requiere servicios de interpretación en Lengua de Señas Peruana (LSP) para asegurar la accesibilidad en eventos, reuniones, capacitaciones, talleres, campañas de comunicación y otras actividades institucionales. Por lo anterior, se establecerá uno o más Acuerdos a Largo Plazo (LTA-LVC). El LTA-LVC es un Acuerdo no vinculante, es decir, no constituye un compromiso para adquirir los servicios. El(los) LTA(s)-LVC se establecerá(n) considerando: i. un período fijo de validez; ii. términos de referencia fijos; y iii. precio(s) unitario(s) fijo(s). El (los) LTA(s)-LVC se establecerá(n) por el período inicial de 1 año con la posibilidad de prórroga por un segundo y posteriormente por un tercer año, siempre y cuando el desempeño del profesional haya sido satisfactorio. El (los) LTA(s)-LVC no excederán los tres años. El (los) LTA(s)-LVC se establecerá por un monto referencial anual. Los servicios serán requeridos de manera periódica, según las necesidades que surjan en las distintas áreas de UNICEF. ACTIVIDADES: • Interpretar de español a Lengua de Señas Peruana y viceversa durante reuniones, talleres, capacitaciones, conferencias, eventos públicos y otras actividades institucionales. • Coordinar previamente con el equipo organizador para conocer los objetivos, agenda, materiales y terminología específica de cada actividad. • Revisar documentación y materiales de referencia proporcionados por UNICEF antes de cada sesión. • Asegurar una interpretación precisa, neutral, ética y culturalmente apropiada. • Mantener estricta confidencialidad respecto a la información manejada durante las actividades. • Participar en reuniones preparatorias cuando sea requerido. • Adaptar la interpretación a formatos virtuales mediante plataformas digitales como Microsoft Teams, Zoom u otras. PRODUCTOS: Enviar un tarifario de: Interpretación de español a Lengua de Señas Peruana y viceversa, detallado y desagregado por: a. 1 hora o fracción de tiempo b. 4 horas de media jornada c. 8 horas de jornada completa d. Modalidad virtual e. Modalidad híbrida • Indicar nombre, teléfono y dirección electrónica de otros intérpretes de lengua de señas peruanas con los que trabaja, los cuales deberán presentar su postulación para ser considerados en este proceso. Los servicios podrán desarrollarse: • De forma presencial en Lima u otras regiones del Perú. • De forma virtual mediante plataformas digitales. • En modalidad híbrida, según las necesidades de UNICEF ESPECIFICACIONES PARA LA ENTREGA DE PRODUCTOS De acuerdo con los servicios solicitados por las áreas temáticas. ESPECIFICACIONES PARA EL PAGO DE HONORARIOS PROFESIONALES • Pagos en moneda local soles. • Pagos por productos a total satisfacción de UNICEF. • Pagos dentro de los 30 días de aprobado el producto y de la recepción del Recibo por Honorarios. SERVICIO A TODO COSTO Los servicios que se realicen contra el LTA-LVC serán a todo costo, por lo que todo gasto no previsto requerido para la realización del servicio será cubierto en su totalidad por el/la profesional. VIAJES De requerirse algún viaje, los costos serán cubiertos por UNICEF. CALIFICACIONES MÍNIMAS REQUERIDAS: Disciplinas: Estudios técnicos, universitarios o certificación especializada en interpretación de Lengua de Señas Peruanas. Conocimientos/Experiencia/Habilidades requeridas • Excelente dominio de la Lengua de Señas Peruana y del idioma español Experiencia en interpretación para eventos institucionales, capacitaciones, conferencias o espacios públicos. • Deseable experiencia de trabajo con organismos internacionales, entidades públicas, organizaciones de la sociedad civil o proyectos de desarrollo. • Habilidades de comunicación interpersonal. A) Evaluación Técnica (Cumple /No Cumple) Factor 1 – Formación académica • Estudios técnicos, universitarios o especialización en interpretación de Lengua de Señas Peruana. • Deseable formación complementaria en discapacidad, inclusión social, derechos humanos o educación inclusiva • Acreditación: CV / P11 o Certificaciones/Diplomas • Rango de valoración: Cumple, No Cumple Factor 2 – Tiempo de experiencia en interpretación de Lengua de Señas Peruanas • Experiencia laboral mínima de dos (2) años realizando interpretación de Lengua de Señas Peruanas • Acreditación: CV / P11 o Contratos y/o Constancias. • Rango de valoración: Cumple, No Cumple Factor 3 – Experiencia con Agencias de Cooperación Internacional, ONGs, instituciones públicas, medios de comunicación y/o afines • Experiencia al haber realizado al menos cinco (5) servicios de interpretación de Lengua de Señas Peruanas en las entidades descritas. • Acreditación: CV / P11 o Contratos y/o Constancias. • Rango de valoración: Cumple, No Cumple B) Evaluación Económica La oferta económica debe ser presentada en moneda local, de acuerdo con lo solicitado anteriormente bajo “Productos”, en el formato en Excel denominado Anexo 1: Anexo 1 - Propuesta Económica - TdRs LTA-LVC Lengua de Señas Peruana SR.xlsx C) Evaluación Final: Evaluación Técnica + Evaluación Económica Se establecerá LTA-LVC con el(los) profesional(es) quien(es) cumpla(n) con lo mínimo solicitado en la parte técnica y presenten una oferta económica conveniente para UNICEF. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Esta plataforma permite adjuntar documentos en formatos .DOC, .DOCx, .PDF, .TXT y links. El CV, la carta de presentación, cualquier documento solicitado para acreditar su formación/experiencia y los certificados que acreditan su educación, deberán ser adjuntados en los siguientes campos: Please upload your C.V. / Resume. Please upload your cover letter Please upload writing sample or list of publication or portfolio of your works that is in line with the assignment described in TOR/Vacancy Announcement Please upload a copy of your highest level of education certificate. Esta plataforma está diseñada para ingresar la propuesta económica USD. Por tanto, indicar el monto de la propuesta económica a todo costo (considerando viajes, si aplica) en USD, en el siguiente campo: Please state your overall fee for the whole assignment including all travel cost related and other expenses related to the assignment. Los consultores deberán presentar su propuesta económica detallada en soles. La propuesta económica detallada, deberá ser adjuntada en el siguiente campo (de no adjuntarse la aplicación no será considerada). Please upload Financial Proposal here (sólo se considerarán las postulaciones que adjunten este campo). Las personas contratadas en el marco de una consultoría o de un contrato individual no serán consideradas "miembros del personal" en virtud del Estatuto y Reglamento del Personal de las Naciones Unidas y de las políticas y procedimientos de UNICEF, y no tendrán derecho a las prestaciones previstas en los mismos (como el derecho a vacaciones y la cobertura del seguro médico). Sus condiciones de servicio se regirán por su contrato y por las Condiciones Generales de Contratación de los Servicios de Consultores y Contratistas Individuales. Los consultores y contratistas individuales son responsables de determinar sus obligaciones fiscales y del pago de cualquier impuesto y/o derecho, de conformidad con la legislación local u otras leyes aplicables. El candidato seleccionado es el único responsable de garantizar que el visado (si procede) y el seguro médico necesarios para desempeñar las funciones del contrato sean válidos durante todo el periodo del contrato. Los candidatos seleccionados están sujetos a la confirmación del estado de vacunación completa contra el SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19) con una vacuna avalada por la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS), que debe cumplirse antes de asumir la misión. No se aplica a los consultores que trabajarán a distancia y de quienes no se espera que trabajen o visiten las instalaciones de UNICEF, los lugares de ejecución de programas o que interactúen directamente con las comunidades con las que trabaja UNICEF, ni que viajen para desempeñar funciones para UNICEF durante la duración de sus contratos de consultoría. UNICEF ofrece ajustes razonables a los consultores con discapacidades. Esto puede incluir, por ejemplo, programas informáticos accesibles, asistencia en viajes de misión o asistentes personales. Le animamos a que revele su discapacidad durante su solicitud por si necesitara adaptaciones razonables durante el proceso de selección y posteriormente en su asignación. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Partnerships Specialist (Philanthropy) (P-3), FT, #00113282, Panama City – Panama, LACRO Apply now Job no: 596033 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Panama City Level: P-3 Location: Panama Categories: Partnerships UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Future Currently UNICEF is operating in a rapidly evolving financing landscape, where traditional humanitarian and development funding sources are becoming more constrained, volatile, and less predictable. At the same time, private sector engagement is evolving, with donors and partners increasingly seeking more strategic, measurable, and co-created forms of collaboration. This presents a significant opportunity for UNICEF in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) to strengthen engagement with the private sector and expand high-value partnerships that can accelerate results for children. In this context, UNICEF is placing greater emphasis on audience-centric engagement strategies to deepen relationships with high-value audiences, including philanthropists, foundations, membership-based organizations (MBOs), and faith-based organizations (FBOs). This shift is particularly relevant in the LAC region, where there is growing potential to unlock greater support from philanthropic actors and mobilize collaborations in the global south. The Private Fundraising and Partnerships (PFP) team in the Latin America and Caribbean Regional Office (LACRO) partners with UNICEF Country Offices (COs) to maximize revenue generation and drive sustainable income growth through strategic fundraising and partnership development across key high-value channels. The team provides integrated strategic oversight, technical expertise, and coordinated guidance to fundraising teams across designated PSFR markets, helping strengthen performance, alignment, and long-term growth. How can you make a difference? The Partnerships Specialist sits within the Latin America and Caribbean Regional Office reporting to the Philanthropy Manager, Private Sector Partnerships (PFP), with close strategic and technical liaison across the PFP and National Committee ecosystem. The postholder will help to drive strategic growth of private philanthropy among high-net-worth individuals, foundations and membership and faith-based organizations in the LAC Region. The postholder will also coordinate effectively with philanthropy fundraisers in PSFR country offices in the region, as well as with the LAC PFP team, offering strategic and technical advice and capacity building, where needed. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Job Description Partnerships Specialist (Philanthropy) (P-3), FT, #00113282, Panama City, Panama.pdf To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education : A completed advanced university degree (i.e. a master's degree or equivalent) in Business Management, Marketing, Finance, International Development, Business Administration, Social Sciences or any other relevant field is required. Work Experience : At least five (5) years of relevant and progressively responsible professional work experience in Philanthropy, Private Sector Partnerships or Fundraising is required. Experience in direct prospecting, relationship cultivation and management of high value philanthropy partnerships is required. Skills : Demonstrated ability to cultivate and strengthen strategic relationships with high-value donors and partners. Demonstrated ability to manage and maintain effective relationships with donors and philanthropic partners. Demonstrated ability to identify, research and assess prospective donors and funding opportunities. Demonstrated ability to negotiate fundraising and partnership arrangements. Demonstrated ability to develop fundraising proposals. Language Requirements : Proficiency in English and intermediate knowledge of Spanish is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French or Russian) is an asset. Relevant work experience in Latin America and the Caribbean region is an asset. Familiarity with and exposure to UNICEF programmes is highly desirable. Relevant experience in managing relationships with high-net-worth individual donors is desirable. Relevant experience in convening philanthropy-related events is desirable. Relevant experience in managing foundation partnerships is desirable. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and their different levels. (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (1) (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (1) (3) Drive to achieve impactful results (1) (4) Innovates and embraces change (1) (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (1) (6) Thinks and acts strategically (1) (7) Works collaboratively with others (1) UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to including everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks, and reasonable accommodation for people with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding, and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection, and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidate's willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female and male candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to staying and delivering in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. The team provides integrated strategic oversight, technical expertise, and coordinated guidance to fundraising teams across designated PSFR markets, helping strengthen performance, alignment, and long-term growth. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Supply Associate, G-6, TA (6months), #138543, Democratic Republic of Congo - WCAR Apply now Job no: 596039 Contract type: Temporary Appointment Duty Station: Bunia Location: Democratic Republic of Congo Categories: Supply Management UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared an outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease affecting Ituri and other affected or at-risk provinces. National authorities, with the support of humanitarian partners, have activated emergency coordination and response mechanisms to contain transmission and protect affected communities. The outbreak is unfolding in a complex humanitarian environment marked by insecurity, population displacement, high mobility, constrained access to essential services and weak water, sanitation, hygiene and infection prevention and control systems. These conditions heighten the risk of transmission in health facilities and communities and require rapid, well-coordinated and technically rigorous WASH/IPC action. The geographic expansion of the outbreak, the operational complexity of the response and the need to align interventions across national, provincial and health-zone levels require senior leadership. An experienced profile is therefore required to provide the strategic expertise, technical authority and convening capacity needed to lead UNICEF's WASH/IPC response and support Government-led coordination across affected and at-risk areas. How can you make a difference? Under the supervision of the Supply Officer, the Supply Associate performs highly skilled procurement and supply work in support of the Ebola emergency response, managing complex procurement and contracting cases and client requests that frequently require evaluation of difficult situations and adaptation of procedures. Working with a high degree of operational independence, the incumbent leads to end-to-end procurement processes and contributes to the design and development of improved supply services and delivery mechanisms. The incumbent may supervise lower-level GS staff. MAJOR DUTIES AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Procurement Services and supply financing (where applicable) Localization and emergency preparedness Information and data management and reporting If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: ToR Supply Associate, GS6,Bunia.docx To qualify as a champion for every child you will have… Education : Completion of secondary education is required with a minimum of six (6) years of relevant administrative experience in logistics, warehousing, transport, supply chain management or a commercial context. A bachelor’s degree from a recognized academic institution in the above fields may replace three years of related work experience. A master’s degree may replace an additional two years. Work Experience: Demonstrated ability to apply UNICEF (or comparable) logistics and supply rules, procedures and good practices to complex individual cases. Experience using an ERP system (VISION/SAP supply and logistics modules) and MS Office tools. Skills: Experience gained in a humanitarian, emergency, or public-health-emergency setting. Experience supporting an active outbreak or emergency response (e.g., Ebola, cholera, measles, mpox, displacement, or a declared L2/L3 emergency), preferably in the Democratic Republic of the Congo or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, and resource-constrained environments. Experience working with and/or through counterparts (Government and decentralized authorities, UN agencies, cluster and coordination mechanisms, implementing partners) to deliver measurable results in insecure or hard-to-reach areas. Experience gained in a humanitarian, emergency, or public-health-emergency setting. Experience supporting an active outbreak or emergency response (e.g., Ebola, cholera, measles, mpox, displacement, or a declared L2/L3 emergency), preferably in the Democratic Republic of the Congo or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, and resource-constrained environments. Experience working with and/or through counterparts (Government and decentralized authorities, UN agencies, cluster and coordination mechanisms, implementing partners) to deliver measurable results in insecure or hard-to-reach areas. Professional and/or university courses related to Procurement (e.g.: CIPS), supply chain management or a related field are highly desirable. Experience in Emergency Response like Ebola Outbreak is highly desirable. UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct.UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable.Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks.Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. This position has been assessed as an elevated risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children’s data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e. UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and working authorization for candidates under consideration for positions at the national officer and general service category. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 W. Central Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 W. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Consultants nationaux départementaux terrai en Engagement Communautaire, Cotonou, 6 months, télétravail+ missions, 596047 Apply now Job no: 596047 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: Cotonou Level: Consultancy Location: Benin Categories: Social and Behavior Change L’UNICEF travaille dans plus de 190 pays et territoires pour sauver la vie des enfants, défendre leurs droits et les aider à réaliser leur plein potentiel, de la petite enfance à l’adolescence. À l’UNICEF, nous sommes engagés, passionnés et fiers de ce que nous faisons, aussi longtemps que notre présence est nécessaire. Promouvoir les droits de chaque enfant n’est pas simplement un métier - c’est une vocation. L’UNICEF est un lieu où les carrières se construisent : nous offrons à notre personnel des opportunités variées de développement professionnel et personnel, leur permettant de renforcer leur sentiment d’utilité tout en servant les enfants et les communautés à travers le monde, avec en prime un ensemble attractif de rémunérations et d’avantages. Nous vous invitons à consulter notre site web (website) pour en savoir plus sur les activités et le mandat de l’UNICEF. Dans le but d'améliorer la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle du pays, le gouvernement du Benin, à travers sa politique nationale, s’est engagé dans la mise en oeuvre du programme de supplémentation nutritionnelle systématique durant les 1000 premiers jours de vie de l'enfant visant à induire une amélioration de la situation nutritionnelle dans les communes dans lesquelles les prévalences de malnutrition sont les plus aigües. Ce programme ambitieux piloté par l’Agence Nationale de l’Alimentation et de la Nutrition en collaboration avec l’Agence Nationale des Soins de Santé Primaire et le Ministère des Affaires Sociales et la Microfinance, a démarré dans 13 communes en 2025 et en cours d’extension pour atteindre 46 communes à fin 2026 ll est prévu à cet effet, le recrutement de dix (10) consultants pour appuyer la cartographie des interventions et intervenants de nutrition y compris les plateformes communautaires, l’analyse des connaissances, pratiques et perceptions des communautés en matière de nutrition et l’appui au déploiement du modèle d’engagement communautaire dans les communes de mise en oeuvre. Les consultants départementaux ont donc comme responsabilité de fournir une assistance technique de proximité aux équipes opérationnelles et partenaires locaux dans les communes participantes pour renforcer les interventions de communication et d'engagement communautaire en faveur du Projet de Supplémentation des 1000 premiers jours. Si vous souhaitez obtenir de plus d’amples informations sur cette consultance, notamment concernant les livrables détaillés et les résultats attendus, veuillez consulter les Termes de Référence complets ici : External ToR TMC0006056.pdf Qualifications minimales requises: Formation académique : Être un spécialiste en communication et avoir un Diplôme d’Etudes Universitaires Supérieures de niveau minimal Bac+5 (Master`s) en communication, sciences sociales ; sciences du comportement (sociologie, anthropologie, psychologie, développement communautaire) Expérience professionnelle: Un minimum de plus de 5 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la planification et la gestion des programmes de communication pour le changement de comportement et social avec une expérience pratique dans l’engagement communautaire en faveur de la nutrition Au moins cinq années d'expérience de travail dans les domaines de la planification et de la gestion des programmes de communication pour le changement social et de comportement, avec une expérience pratique dans la participation et l’engagement communautaire. Expériences avérées dans l’élaboration de plan de communication et la mise en place de base de données. Une expérience dans les interventions de promotion de la nutrition Expériences dans le suivi, l’évaluation des interventions de communication ou dans un domaine reconnu équivalent. Une expertise avérée dans la conception d’outil de suivi et évaluation en communication serait un atout Exigences linguistiques: Excellente connaissance du français La maîtrise d’une ou deux langues des départements à charge est un atout Atouts souhaités : Une expérience de travail avec le SYSTHEME DES NATION UNIES et la possession d’un permis de conduire A constitueraient des atouts Pour chaque enfant, vous devez démontrer... Les valeurs fondamentales de l'UNICEF, à savoir la bienveillance, le respect, l'intégrité, la confiance, la responsabilité et la durabilité (CRITAS). Elles sont à la base de tout ce que nous faisons et de la manière dont nous le faisons. Découvrez notre Charte des valeurs : Valeurs de l'UNICEF L'UNICEF est là pour servir les enfants les plus défavorisés du monde et notre personnel doit refléter la diversité de ces enfants. L'UNICEF s'est engagé à inclure tout le monde, indépendamment de la race/l'ethnie, de l'âge, du handicap, de l'identité sexuelle, de l'orientation sexuelle, de la religion, de la nationalité, de l'origine socio-économique ou de toute autre caractéristique personnelle. Nous proposons un large éventail de mesures visant à inclure une main-d'œuvre plus diversifiée, comme le congé parental payé, les heures pour allaitement et des aménagements raisonnables pour les personnes handicapées. L'UNICEF encourage vivement le recours à des modalités de travail flexibles. Selon la Convention des Nations Unies relative aux droits des personnes vivant avec un handicap (UNCRPD), les personnes vivant avec un handicap comprennent celles qui présentent des déficiences physiques, mentales, intellectuelles ou sensorielles durables qui, en interaction avec diverses barrières, peuvent faire obstacle à leur pleine et effective participation à la société sur la base de l'égalité avec les autres. L'UNICEF s'engage à promouvoir la protection et la sauvegarde de tous les enfants. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront l'objet d'une vérification rigoureuse de leurs références et de leurs antécédents et devront adhérer à ces normes et principes. Le contrôle des antécédents comprendra la vérification des titres universitaires et des antécédents professionnels. Les candidats sélectionnés peuvent être amenés à fournir des informations supplémentaires pour la vérification de leurs antécédents, et les candidats vivant avec handicap sélectionnés peuvent être invités à soumettre des documents justificatifs relatifs à leur handicap de manière confidentielle. Par ailleurs, l’UNICEF ne demandera jamais les coordonnées bancaires des candidat(e)s. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Procurement Services Manager, P-4, Fixed Term Position, Supply Division, Copenhagen, Denmark, #00021902 Apply now Job no: 596052 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Copenhagen Level: P-4 Location: Denmark Categories: Supply Management UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Champion UNICEF Supply Division (SD) works to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential supplies and services for children and their families, in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts. These supplies are critical to saving lives, supporting children’s health and education, and protecting them from abuse, exploitation, and neglect. As the UN’s largest end to end supply chain entity, UNICEF leverages its global reach, market influence, supply chain expertise and partnerships with governments, civil society, private sector, industry, and other stakeholders to meet children’s needs and protect their rights around the world. SD focuses on three result areas to maximize impact, scale, and effectiveness: strategic procurement; supply preparedness and response in humanitarian and fragile contexts; and supply chain optimization. To facilitate and accelerate progress toward these results, SD employs three change strategies: financing for supply and services, supply chain digitalization and supply chain localization. Develop and maintain a strategic framework for the identification of procurement services projects. Analyse and prioritise Procurement Services activities. Share and engage in the opportunities with UNICEF Regional Offices and Country Offices (RO/CO) through joint training and orientation workshops, visits and correspondence. Initiate new Procurement Services projects jointly with UNICEF HQ and RO/CO and customers, through innovative partnerships at the conceptual stage. Develop a system for progress and results monitoring. Propose corrective action when needed. Develop the communication and advocacy strategies and plans. Co-ordinate and implement the communication plans. This includes all components in the communication mix, such as brochures, infosheets, PowerPoint, Internet, presentation kits, letters (especially promotional) and the customer database. Ensure the development and maintenance of Procurement Services site usability and functionality. Ensure the development of web application of cost estimates. Implement e-procurement in accordance with UNICEF strategy. Take advantage of the internet for strategic communication. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Procurement Services Manager_P4 To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in Business Administration, Management, and any other related fields. Work Experience: 8 years of progressively responsible professional work experience in marketing or leading customer-service teams or related field with 2-3 years, demonstrated experience in managing large, multi-stakeholder projects. Skills: Analytical, negotiation, and advocacy skills. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Excellent computer skills including internet navigation and publishing applications. Language Requirements: Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values The UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others (8) Nurtures, leads and manages people Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. For every child, the right to education Purpose of Activity/Assignment: Generation Unlimited (GenU) Generation Unlimited is UNICEF's global multi-sector partnership platform to connect every young person to employability skilling, employment and entrepreneurship by 2030. By mobilising public, private and youth partners, GenU supports country-level solutions and global offers that strengthen learning-to-earning pathways, with a focus on equity, inclusion and scale. Youth Livelihoods Strategy Alignment This assignment is anchored in the UNICEF Youth Livelihoods Strategy (2026-2029). The Strategy positions youth livelihoods as central to breaking intergenerational poverty by ensuring that investments in education, skills, social protection and other services translate into income, resilience and opportunity for young people and their households. It positions UNICEF to act earlier, act systemically and act at scale, with deliberate attention to adolescent girls, young women, young people with disabilities and other marginalised groups. Strategic Chapeau for the Assignment The consultancy will help operationalise the Strategy across Asia by translating it into practical country and regional products. The work will align with the Strategy's three pillars: systems, policies and data; skills and pathways; and entrepreneurship, income and economic inclusion. It will also reflect the joint ESP-GenU technical assistance model, in which ESP provides the policy, systems and diagnostics backbone, while GenU mobilises partnerships, private sector engagement, financing, innovation and opportunity creation. Role Overview: GenU Senior Partnerships and Youth Livelihoods Consultant - Asia The Consultant will provide senior technical programme, partnership and resource mobilisation support over a 4.5-month period, from 15 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, to consolidate GenU's contribution to the Youth Livelihoods Strategy across priority countries in Asia. Building on existing engagement with country offices, regional colleagues, ESP colleagues and GenU teams, the Consultant will prepare document-based products that can be reviewed and certified within the contract period: a strategy alignment note and pipeline tracker, country investment packages, partnership and financing products, a strategic engagement and capacity support package, and a final handover package with an Asia youth livelihoods roadmap for 2027. How can you make a difference? Fluency in English (written and spoken) is necessary Working knowledge of other UN official languages is an asset. Youth livelihoods strategy, partnership architecture, proposal and pitch development, CPD/UNSDCF integration, private sector engagement, public-private-youth partnership models, blended finance concepts, pipeline management, project management and remote coordination across multiple time zones. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors.UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations.This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities. How can you make a difference? The health system is under considerable strain, with capacities for isolation, rapid diagnosis, and case management sometimes being limited. Challenges related to specimen collection, transportation, and analysis, as well as delays in reporting and validating data, can hinder the timely confirmation of cases and the rapid implementation of control measures. The operational context remains particularly complex, marked by persistent insecurity, population displacement, inter-provincial mobility, and limited humanitarian access in certain areas. These constraints are further compounded by mistrust among some communities toward the health system, the spread of rumors, and delayed recourse to healthcare facilities or reliance on traditional practices. These factors can delay the reporting of alerts, the isolation of suspected cases, and the effective monitoring of contacts. Work Experience: At least two (2) years of relevant professional experience in community-based surveillance or public health programs. Skills: Good knowledge of epidemiological surveillance Proficiency in Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) approaches Knowledge of the community context and local dynamics Ability to work effectively with community stakeholders Strong supervision and training skills Competencies in routine and mass vaccination activities Good knowledge of epidemiological surveillance Proficiency in Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) approaches Knowledge of the community context and local dynamics Ability to work effectively with community stakeholders Strong supervision and training skills Competencies in routine and mass vaccination activities Language Requirements: Proficiency in French is required. Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). Intermediate knowledge of English and national languages, particularly Swahili, is considered an asset. Experience in outbreak response (such as Ebola, cholera, or other infectious disease outbreaks) is considered an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts.
